# dsh-avatar-chat
Dual avatars for the DeepSeek Harness chat transcript — a user avatar on the right of every user tur
n, an assistant avatar on the left of every answer — plus an **Avatars** page in Settings to switch
each side on or off, set a picture, and pick the size.
A DSH Web Client plugin: a Cordis bundle that registers one `settings.section` seat and decorates th
e transcript with a page-level stylesheet.
## Quick start
Three ways in, easiest first. **Plugin market** — switch on **Plugins → More → Experimental plugins
→ Custom plugin markets**, add this source under **Discover**, and install the card:

**One command** — quit the app first, then:

**From the app** — **Plugins → Add plugin** in the sidebar, same spec. Restart DeepSeek Harness eith
er way. Details in Install.
## Screenshots
Transcript — the user's picture beside the request on the right, the assistant's beside the reply on
the left, both at 50 px:
Settings — the **Avatars** page this plugin adds, with a picture chosen on each side:
Both come from the author's own desktop build (Chinese locale, custom wallpaper); the pictures, the
size, and the toggles are exactly the controls the page exposes.
## Features
- **Two independent avatars.** The user side and the assistant side each have their own visibility t

oggle, their own picture, and their own restore-to-default.
- **Pictures from disk or from a URL.**
Upload PNG / JPEG / WebP / GIF (max 5 MiB, downscaled to 256 px), or paste an `https://…` address. T

he address is probed once before it is adopted.
- **Built-in look with no picture at all.** With no
upload, each side draws a pure-CSS disc using theme tokens only — no bundled image, no literal colou

r, correct in light and dark.
- **Size from 20 px to 64 px**, applied live to both the transcript an

d the settings preview.
- **Undecorated where it should be.** One assistant reply is split into a re

asoning row and a response row; only the answer row carries an avatar, so a reply never shows two.
-
**Clean unload.** Every root attribute and custom property the plugin writes is removed when the pl
* Every root attribute and custom property the plugin writes is removed when the plugin is disposed.
## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-alpha.4` (Web / Desktop). The plugin uses only the shipped theme tokens an

d the `settings.section` slot.
- The four modules the bundle requires at runtime — `react`, `react/j
sx-runtime`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` — are all part
of the shell's frozen module table, so nothing extra needs installing next to this package.
## Install
A profile-local plugin joins a profile as a **bundle**: its `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patc
h`, and the profile lists the package name in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The profile's own `cordis.patch
.yml` is *id-targeted* — it can only override or disable an entry a bundle layer already declared —
so adding a row there installs nothing.
## Storage and privacy
Preferences live in the browser's `localStorage` under the single key `dsh.avatar-chat.v1`, as JSON:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- Uploaded pictures are stored as **data URLs** — they never leave the browser, and they are never w

ritten into the session log.
- The value is **plain text in origin-shared storage**: any script on t

he same origin can read it. Do not upload anything you would not put in a local file.
- Reads and wr
ites are individually guarded. A denied origin, an exhausted quota, or a damaged value degrades to i

n-memory preferences plus an on-page notice instead of breaking the plugin load.
- A document with a
foreign `schemaVersion`, an out-of-range size, or a malformed side is repaired in place and reporte
emaVersion`, an out-of-range size, or a malformed side is repaired in place and reported as damaged.
## How it works
DSH has no slot that adds leading or trailing chrome to an individual chat message row: `conversatio
n.chat.node`'s keyed seats are already fully occupied by the shipped renderers (`user`, `steering`,
`assistant-step`, …) and a third-party package cannot import or wrap them. Every class name inside t
he chat subtree is also a CSS-Modules hash, so it is not addressable from another package.
What *is* stable is the row element itself, which carries `data-chat-flow-kind` (equal to the chat n
ode kind), `data-chat-turn`, and `data-chat-group-part`. So the plugin ships a page-level stylesheet
that selects on those attributes, and drives it entirely from root-element state:

- attributes `data-dsh-avatar-chat`, `-user`, `-user-image`, `-assistant`, `-assistant-image`
- cust
om properties `--dsh-avatar-chat-size` and the two picture variables
The avatar is painted by an absolutely-positioned `::before` inside padding the stylesheet reserves
on the decorated row; the row keeps its shipped `display`, so host layout is untouched.
The stylesheet is a plain `.css` side-effect import, which the DSH client bundler turns into a tagge
d `<style data-plugin-css>` element — deduplicated by tag id, so re-running the plugin never double-
injects it. Every root write is absolute, so applying twice is idempotent.
## Known limitations
- The decoration depends on `data-chat-flow-kind`, which is **not a published contract**. If the cha

t row markup changes, avatars disappear silently until the selector is updated.
- Only `user`, `stee
ring` and `assistant-step` rows are decorated. Tool calls, commands, system prompts and turn-process

rows have no avatar.
- A decorated row becomes `position: relative`, so it is the containing block

for its own absolutely-positioned descendants.
- The avatar carries no per-message identity — there

is exactly one user picture and one assistant picture at a time.
- A remote picture address is probe

d once when it is applied and is not revalidated afterwards.
- The built-in disc uses `--dsw-alias-b
rand-primary`, which is near-black in light mode and near-white in dark mode — an inverse monochrome
accent, not a brand blue.
## Compatibility
Verified against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-alpha.4` on Windows with the shipped Web client, in both un
it tests and a real headless-Chromium run against an assembled profile.
